description: A 16-good master population with variable category cardinality and 16 diverse bidder archetypes. Auction experiments sample at most 10 goods and 10 bidders.

goods.description: High-performance 16-core desktop processor for demanding gaming, creative, and compute workloads.
Balanced 8-core desktop processor offering strong general-purpose performance.
Entry-level 4-core desktop processor for basic productivity and budget systems.
Professional accelerator with high VRAM capacity for AI training and technical compute.
High-end gaming graphics card for high-resolution and high-frame-rate play.
Value-oriented graphics card for mainstream gaming and light acceleration.
128GB high-speed memory kit for large professional, server, and AI workloads.
64GB high-speed memory kit for demanding multitasking, gaming, and creation.
32GB mainstream memory kit for general productivity and gaming.
Workstation motherboard with robust power delivery, expansion, and high-speed connectivity.
Mainstream motherboard suitable for ordinary desktop builds.
High-performance 4TB NVMe solid-state drive for large datasets and media libraries.
Fast 2TB NVMe solid-state drive for applications, games, and everyday storage.
Efficient 1000W modular power supply for high-performance components.
High-capacity all-in-one liquid CPU cooler for sustained demanding workloads.
Well-ventilated ATX chassis supporting the available motherboards and full-size components.

bidder_profiles.role: A competitive gaming buyer assembling one premium desktop for high frame rates, low latency, and sustained performance. Premium graphics, processing, power, and cooling receive the highest valuations.
bidder_profiles.identity_text: A long-time competitive gamer who regularly participates in online tournaments and organised team play.

substitute_groups.description: Alternative processors for the single gaming-system CPU socket; the high-end option commands a substantial performance premium.
Mutually exclusive primary gaming-card choices for one desktop build.
Alternative matched memory configurations for the same gaming system.

complement_groups.description: A balanced high-frame-rate platform in which the chassis and power supply support the flagship processing components.
Robust motherboard power delivery and liquid cooling enable the premium processor to sustain boost performance.
Fast memory and storage complement the high-end graphics card for competitive games and large modern titles.

bidder_profiles.notes: Values a single optimized gaming system rather than spare professional or entry-level parts.

bidder_profiles.role: A budget-focused desktop buyer comparing complete configurations by playable performance per dollar. Mainstream parts are preferred, while premium alternatives retain limited value when deeply discounted.
bidder_profiles.identity_text: A recreational gamer who spends evenings playing mainstream multiplayer and single-player games with friends.

substitute_groups.description: Three processor tiers compete for the sole CPU position in a price-constrained gaming build.
Alternative primary gaming cards, with the value card offering the preferred performance-per-dollar balance.
Alternative matched memory-kit capacities for one desktop; surplus kits provide no meaningful benefit to this buyer.

complement_groups.description: A complete, cost-effective mainstream gaming platform with balanced component capabilities.
The high-end graphics alternative becomes more practical when paired with sufficient power and a ventilated chassis.
Improved cooling and fast storage make the preferred midrange processor configuration more responsive and comfortable to use.

bidder_profiles.notes: Strongly discounts expensive capacity and enthusiast features that do not materially improve ordinary gaming.

bidder_profiles.role: A dual-purpose buyer building a workstation for high-quality gameplay, live encoding, and post-production. Large memory, fast storage, and both gaming and compute acceleration can contribute to the production workflow.
bidder_profiles.identity_text: A livestreamer and video creator who broadcasts gameplay and produces edited recordings for an online audience.

substitute_groups.description: Alternative processors for the single production workstation, with the high-core option preferred for simultaneous encoding and editing.
Either accelerator can fill the primary graphics role, while an additional card retains partial value for rendering, AI-assisted editing, or a secondary production system.
Alternative matched memory capacities for the main streaming workstation; one complete kit is selected.

complement_groups.description: A high-throughput streaming and gaming platform able to sustain gameplay, capture, and encoding concurrently.
A professional content-production subsystem for AI-assisted tools, large editing projects, and accelerated rendering.
Fast working storage and a ventilated full-size chassis support reliable game capture with the premium gaming card.

bidder_profiles.notes: Can exploit a secondary accelerator, but derives little value from entry-level processors or mainstream motherboard limitations.

bidder_profiles.role: A hardware experimenter purchasing components for tuning, comparative benchmarking, and documented test builds. Multiple alternatives retain value because they can be evaluated in separate configurations rather than merely stored as backups.
bidder_profiles.identity_text: A desktop-hardware hobbyist who enjoys assembling systems, experimenting with configurations, and documenting benchmark results.

substitute_groups.description: Processor tiers are comparable benchmark subjects, and additional CPUs retain value for separate tuning configurations.
The two accelerator classes enable comparative gaming, compute, thermal, and efficiency benchmarks across multiple test configurations.
Multiple memory capacities and kits support capacity-scaling, timing, and overclocking experiments in different builds.

complement_groups.description: A complete high-power CPU overclocking platform with robust delivery, thermal headroom, and suitable airflow.
The professional accelerator becomes a viable compute benchmark platform when paired with expansion capacity, power headroom, and ventilation.
A complete inexpensive control system for baseline comparisons against tuned premium hardware.

bidder_profiles.notes: Values broad component variety for active testing, but marginal value declines once enough parts are available to populate several benchmark configurations.

bidder_profiles.role: A cost-conscious student comparing a mainstream study-and-gaming build with a grant-supported local research-compute configuration. The system must remain useful for coursework even without premium components.
bidder_profiles.identity_text: A university student who uses a desktop for coursework, research, communication, and occasional games.

substitute_groups.description: Only one processor is needed for the student's single desktop, with the choice balancing cost and performance.
The budget supports one graphics path: research acceleration or affordable general graphics.
One memory kit is sufficient, and capacity is selected according to the chosen research or mainstream configuration.

complement_groups.description: An affordable and balanced coursework system with enough graphics capability for occasional games.
A coherent local research-compute configuration with memory, storage, expansion, and power support for the accelerator.

bidder_profiles.notes: Strongly budget constrained; premium research hardware is relevant primarily when external funding or a substantial discount is available.

bidder_profiles.role: An employee seeking a dependable productivity desktop, while considering a privacy-preserving local AI configuration for sensitive document and spreadsheet workflows. Responsiveness, stability, and low disruption matter more than gaming performance.
bidder_profiles.identity_text: An office employee whose working day involves documents, spreadsheets, web applications, and video meetings.

substitute_groups.description: The office desktop requires one processor, with the lower-cost option adequate for routine work and the midrange option improving responsiveness.
A single memory kit is chosen according to whether the machine handles ordinary multitasking or larger local analytical workloads.

complement_groups.description: A reliable mainstream office platform for documents, web applications, meetings, and routine multitasking.
A supported local AI workstation path with sufficient memory, expansion, power, and chassis capacity.
A responsive higher-capacity productivity configuration for heavy spreadsheets and concurrent applications.

bidder_profiles.notes: The professional accelerator has value only for an approved local-AI workflow; otherwise the bidder favors the conventional office configuration.

bidder_profiles.role: A household buyer balancing schoolwork, administration, media, games, and experimentation by several family members. The preferred purchase is a versatile mainstream system, with premium parts considered only when they materially extend its useful life.
bidder_profiles.identity_text: A household organiser arranging a shared desktop for schoolwork, home administration, entertainment, and family use.

substitute_groups.description: The shared household desktop needs one processor, selected according to the final budget and expected service life.
The family will install one graphics option, choosing between premium play and affordable mainstream gaming.
One memory kit is sufficient for the shared computer, with the larger capacity offering diminishing benefits for ordinary family use.

complement_groups.description: A firm-budget family configuration suitable for schoolwork, household administration, media, and mainstream games.
A versatile entertainment and productivity system with ample storage for games, photos, and family media.

bidder_profiles.notes: The household values flexibility but will not buy duplicate processors, graphics cards, or memory kits for a single shared computer.

bidder_profiles.role: A light user purchasing only a compact set of conventional desktop parts for communication, writing, browsing, and records. Extra performance has little value unless it simplifies the build or is obtained at negligible additional cost.
bidder_profiles.identity_text: A light computer user whose routine consists mainly of email, browsing, writing, and managing personal records.

substitute_groups.description: Only one processor is useful in the simple desktop, and the entry-level model already satisfies nearly all routine needs.

complement_groups.description: A complete, uncomplicated desktop foundation tailored to email, browsing, writing, and personal administration.
A slightly more responsive alternative platform when the midrange processor is available at a modest premium.

bidder_profiles.notes: The accelerator has only nominal option value if bundled nearly free; it does not justify displacing any essential mainstream component.

bidder_profiles.role: Runs local machine-learning experiments and values accelerator capacity, large memory, sustained compute, and fast dataset access.
bidder_profiles.identity_text: A machine-learning researcher who develops experiments, trains models, and analyses results locally.

substitute_groups.description: Alternative processors for the research workstation; only one processor can be installed in the selected motherboard.
Both cards can accelerate compatible workloads, while a second heterogeneous GPU retains value for auxiliary experiments and visualisation.
Alternative memory configurations for one workstation, with the 128GB kit strongly preferred.
Either drive can host datasets, while acquiring both adds useful independent capacity for active data and checkpoints.

complement_groups.description: A balanced accelerator platform with sufficient host memory, expansion support, and power delivery.
A sustained preprocessing and model-development subsystem with ample memory, dataset storage, and cooling.
Compatible workstation infrastructure that can safely house and support demanding components.

bidder_profiles.notes: Places exceptional value on the professional accelerator and 128GB memory; lower-capacity components mainly serve as fallbacks.

bidder_profiles.role: Builds a high-throughput editing and rendering workstation for client video, photography, effects, and final delivery.
bidder_profiles.identity_text: An independent media professional who edits long-form video, processes photographs, and delivers finished productions to clients.

substitute_groups.description: Alternative processors for the single editing workstation, with the high-end processor preferred for exports and encoding.
Either GPU supports creative acceleration, while owning both retains value by separating professional rendering from real-time preview and display workloads.
Alternative memory capacities for the editing workstation; simultaneous kits provide little dependable value compared with the preferred validated configuration.
Multiple drives remain valuable as separate media, cache, and project-delivery volumes.

complement_groups.description: A responsive high-resolution editing system with strong playback, effects, memory, and media throughput.
A professional rendering configuration with sufficient memory, expansion, and power.
A properly powered and cooled chassis configuration for sustained client exports.
Separate high-speed project and cache volumes improve workflow organisation and throughput.

bidder_profiles.notes: Values both available high-performance GPUs because they suit different creative applications, but has no meaningful demand for entry-level components.

bidder_profiles.role: Needs a flexible local development machine for compilation, containers, virtual machines, automated tests, and several concurrent services.
bidder_profiles.identity_text: A software developer who works on several codebases and routinely runs development environments, automated tests, and local services.

substitute_groups.description: Three processor tiers for a single development host; only one can occupy the motherboard socket.
Alternative memory configurations for one host, with 64GB offering the preferred balance for containers and virtual machines.
Alternative motherboards for the same development machine, so acquiring both offers no meaningful benefit.
Either SSD can hold repositories and virtual-machine images, while both remain useful as separate system and workspace volumes.

complement_groups.description: A cost-effective primary development platform for compilation, containers, and local services.
A higher-capacity alternative for large builds and numerous concurrent virtual machines.
Supporting infrastructure for a quiet, reliable machine under long compilation and test workloads.
A practical desktop configuration supporting GPU-enabled testing and ordinary multi-monitor development.

bidder_profiles.notes: Prioritises CPU, memory, and storage over graphics performance; entry-level options retain limited fallback value.

bidder_profiles.role: Uses a memory-rich analytical workstation to clean large datasets, run statistical models, and generate reports and visualisations.
bidder_profiles.identity_text: A data analyst who prepares datasets, runs statistical workflows, and produces reports and visualisations.

substitute_groups.description: Alternative processors for one analytical workstation, with either providing sufficient general-purpose compute at a different performance level.
Both GPUs can support visualisation or accelerated analysis, while a second card retains modest value for display duties and separate compatible tasks.
Alternative memory capacities for one workstation, with 128GB preferred for keeping large working datasets resident.
Alternative motherboards for the same workstation build.
Both drives retain value when divided between source datasets, temporary transformations, and reporting outputs.

complement_groups.description: A memory- and storage-heavy platform suited to large local analytical datasets.
An accelerated analysis configuration with adequate host memory and fast local data access.
A stable enclosure, power, and cooling platform for sustained statistical computation.
A lower-cost reporting and visualisation workstation assembled from mainstream components.

bidder_profiles.notes: Strongly prioritises memory and fast local storage; accelerator demand depends on whether analytical tools support GPU execution.

bidder_profiles.role: Procures a broad mix of components for resale to customers with budget, gaming, and professional requirements. Multiple alternatives retain substantial inventory value.
bidder_profiles.identity_text: An independent component reseller who maintains inventory and supplies parts to a varied base of local customers.

substitute_groups.description: Processors serve different customer price tiers, so additional models remain highly marketable inventory.
The accelerator, premium gaming card, and value card address distinct resale segments while substituting for the graphics slot in individual builds.
Memory capacities are alternatives within a single build but all retain strong resale value across customer tiers.
Professional and mainstream boards support separate workstation and ordinary desktop orders.
Both storage capacities can be resold independently or installed together in premium systems.

complement_groups.description: A coordinated premium gaming inventory package can be sold as the foundation of a high-end build.
These components form the core of a professional AI workstation package with strong resale appeal.
A balanced mainstream component set can be marketed as an affordable complete-build foundation.
The board, cooling, power, and chassis support reliable deployment of the high-performance processor.

bidder_profiles.notes: Values reflect expected resale proceeds net of handling risk; inventory remains useful across multiple customer orders.

bidder_profiles.role: Procures dependable parts for employee workstation replacements, upgrades, and a limited stock of spares. Values standardized mainstream components over specialized accelerators.
bidder_profiles.identity_text: An IT administrator responsible for maintaining desktop systems used by employees at a small business.

substitute_groups.description: The processors are alternatives for a given workstation, but both can be deployed across machines with different performance needs.
Different memory capacities support power users and ordinary office employees, with extra kits useful for upgrades.
The mainstream board fits standard replacements while the professional board remains useful for a more demanding employee workstation.
Both drives can be deployed to separate desktops or combined where local working storage is important.

complement_groups.description: A dependable employee workstation core with sufficient memory and fast local storage.
A robust platform for a sustained-use technical or managerial workstation.
A practical content and visualization upgrade set for an employee who handles larger media or design workloads.

bidder_profiles.notes: Specialized AI and premium gaming hardware has no material value for the current employee fleet.

bidder_profiles.role: Builds and expands a home server environment for virtual machines, storage, media services, and development workloads. Additional compatible components can support redundancy or separate server nodes.
bidder_profiles.identity_text: A self-hosting enthusiast who operates personal services, development tools, and media applications from a home server.

substitute_groups.description: Processors compete for a given server node but can also power separate primary, backup, or low-load systems.
Memory kits provide alternative capacities and can be allocated across multiple server nodes or retained for expansion.
The professional board is preferred for the main server while the standard board can support a secondary node.
Both drives retain substantial value because they can expand the same storage pool, host separate workloads, or provide redundancy.

complement_groups.description: A high-capacity virtualization and storage server core with sufficient power and expansion support.
A balanced secondary server node for routine self-hosted services and development tools.
Power, motherboard, and chassis support reliable sustained operation of the high-end processor.
A media-server package that combines light acceleration with ample memory and local storage.

bidder_profiles.notes: Gaming and professional AI GPUs are omitted because their acquisition costs exceed their utility for the operator's current services.

bidder_profiles.role: Acquires components for multiple client builds ranging from basic desktops to gaming and AI workstations. Alternatives remain valuable because they can be assigned to different client orders.
bidder_profiles.identity_text: A small system integrator who assembles and configures desktop machines for several kinds of client.

substitute_groups.description: Each processor tier can satisfy a different client order, so acquiring multiple tiers preserves most of their value.
The GPUs are alternatives within individual configurations but serve professional compute, premium gaming, and mainstream clients.
All three memory capacities are useful across separate workstation, gaming, and ordinary desktop contracts.
Both boards retain strong deployment value for different client reliability and expansion requirements.
The drives can be allocated to different builds or combined in a storage-intensive workstation.

complement_groups.description: A cohesive AI and technical-compute workstation core suitable for a high-value professional contract.
A premium gaming configuration gains substantial client value from matched performance and thermal capacity.
A balanced mainstream machine can be sold as an affordable turnkey client system.
These parts form the foundation of a dependable entry-level productivity desktop.
A robust professional platform combines sustained processing, expansion, fast storage, power, and cooling.

bidder_profiles.notes: Values include expected assembly-margin opportunities and the flexibility to assign inventory across active client projects.
